Removing it from a diff only re-creates the uncommitted change; committing it with your work keeps the tree clean. 58 59 60 ``` 61 62 ## Using the codemod 63 64 To update to Next.js version 16, you can use the `upgrade` [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#160): 65 66 ```bash package="pnpm" 67 pnpm dlx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest 68 ``` 69 70 ```bash package="npm" 71 npx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest 72 ``` 73 74 ```bash package="yarn" 75 yarn dlx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest 76 ``` 77 78 ```bash package="bun" 79 bunx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest 80 ``` 81 82 The [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#160) is able to: 83 84 - Update `next.config.js` to use the new `turbopack` configuration 85 - Migrate from `next lint` to the ESLint CLI 86 - Migrate from deprecated `middleware` convention to `proxy` 87 - Remove `unstable_` prefix from stabilized APIs 88 - Remove `experimental_ppr` Route Segment Config from pages and layouts 89 90 The `upgrade` codemod does not run every migration codemod. If your app still uses synchronous `params`, `searchParams`, `cookies()`, `headers()`, or `draftMode()` access from the Next.js 15 compatibility period, also run the async Request APIs codemod: 91 92 ```bash filename="Terminal" 93 npx @next/codemod@canary next-async-request-api . 94 ``` 95 96 ## Install packages manually 97 98 If you prefer to do it manually, install the latest Next.js and React versions: 99 100 ```bash package="pnpm" 101 pnpm add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 102 ``` 103 104 ```bash package="npm" 105 npm install next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 106 ``` 107 108 ```bash package="yarn" 109 yarn add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 110 ``` 111 112 ```bash package="bun" 113 bun add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 114 ``` 115 116 If you are using TypeScript, ensure you also upgrade `@types/react` and `@types/react-dom` to their latest versions. 117 118 ## Node.js runtime and browser support 119 120 | Requirement | Change / Details | 121 | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | 122 | Node.js 20.9+ | Minimum version now `20.9.0` (LTS); Node.js 18 no longer supported | 123 | TypeScript 5+ | Minimum version now `5.1.0` | 124 | Browsers | Chrome 111+, Edge 111+, Firefox 111+, Safari 16.4+ | 125 126 ## Turbopack by default 127 128 Starting with **Next.js 16**, Turbopack is stable and used by default with `next dev` and `next build` 129 130 Previously you had to enable Turbopack using `--turbopack`, or `--turbo`. 131 132 ```json filename="package.json" 133 { 134 "scripts": { 135 "dev": "next dev --turbopack", 136 "build": "next build --turbopack", 137 "start": "next start" 138 } 139 } 140 ``` 141 142 This is no longer necessary. You can update your `package.json` scripts: 143 144 ```json filename="package.json" 145 { 146 "scripts": { 147 "dev": "next dev", 148 "build": "next build", 149 "start": "next start" 150 } 151 } 152 ``` 153 154 If your project has a [custom `webpack`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/webpack) configuration and you run `next build` (which now uses Turbopack by default), the build will **fail** to prevent misconfiguration issues. 155 156 You have a few different ways to address this: 157 158 - **Use Turbopack anyway:** Run with `next build --turbopack` to build using Turbopack and ignore your `webpack` config. 159 - **Switch to Turbopack fully:** Migrate your `webpack` config to Turbopack-compatible options. 160 - **Keep using Webpack:** Use the `--webpack` flag to opt out of Turbopack and build with Webpack. 161 162 > **Good to know**: If you see failing builds because a `webpack` configuration was found, but you don't define one yourself, it is likely that a plugin is adding a `webpack` option 163 164 ### Opting out of Turbopack 165 166 If you need to continue using Webpack, you can opt out with the `--webpack` flag. For example, to use Turbopack in development but Webpack for production builds: 167 168 ```json filename="package.json" 169 { 170 "scripts": { 171 "dev": "next dev", 172 "build": "next build --webpack", 173 "start": "next start" 174 } 175 } 176 ``` 177 178 We recommend using Turbopack for development and production. Submit a comment to this [thread](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/77721), if you are unable to switch to Turbopack. 179 180 ### Turbopack configuration location 181 182 The `experimental.turbopack` configuration is out of experimental. 183 184 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 185 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 186 187 // Next.js 15 - experimental.turbopack 188 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 189 experimental: { 190 turbopack: { 191 // options 192 }, 193 }, 194 } 195 196 export default nextConfig 197 ``` 198 199 You can use it as a top-level `turbopack` option: 200 201 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 202 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 203 204 // Next.js 16 - turbopack at the top level of nextConfig 205 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 206 turbopack: { 207 // options 208 }, 209 } 210 211 export default nextConfig 212 ``` 213 214 Make sure to review the `Turbopack` configuration [options](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/turbopack). **Next.js 16** introduces various improvements and new options, for example: 215 216 - [Advanced Webpack loader conditions](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/turbopack#advanced-webpack-loader-conditions) 217 - [debugIds](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/turbopack#debug-ids) 218 219 ### Resolve alias fallback 220 221 In some projects, client-side code may import files containing Node.js native modules. This will cause `Module not found: Can't resolve 'fs'` type of errors. 222 223 When this happens, you should refactor your code so that your client-side bundles do not reference these Node.js native modules. 224 225 However, in some cases, this might not be possible. In Webpack the `resolve.fallback` option was typically used to **silence** the error. Turbopack offers a similar option, using `turbopack.resolveAlias`. In this case, tell Turbopack to load an empty module when `fs` is requested for the browser. 226 227 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 228 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 229 230 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 231 turbopack: { 232 resolveAlias: { 233 fs: { 234 browser: './empty.ts', // We recommend to fix code imports before using this method 235 }, 236 }, 237 }, 238 } 239 240 export default nextConfig 241 ``` 242 243 It is preferable to refactor your modules so that client code doesn't ever import from modules using Node.js native modules. 244 245 ### Sass node_modules imports 246 247 Turbopack fully supports importing Sass files from `node_modules`. Note that while Webpack allowed the legacy tilde (`~`) prefix, Turbopack does not support this syntax. 248 249 In Webpack: 250 251 ```scss filename="styles/globals.scss" 252 @import '~bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css'; 253 ``` 254 255 In Turbopack: 256 257 ```scss filename="styles/globals.scss" 258 @import 'bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css'; 259 ``` 260 261 If changing the imports is not possible, you can use `turbopack.resolveAlias`. For example: 262 263 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 264 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 265 266 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 267 turbopack: { 268 resolveAlias: { 269 '~*': '*', 270 }, 271 }, 272 } 273 274 export default nextConfig 275 ``` 276 277 ### Turbopack File System Caching 278 279 Turbopack stores compiler artifacts on disk between runs, for significantly faster compile times across restarts. Filesystem caching is enabled by default for both `next dev` and `next build`, through `experimental.turbopackFileSystemCacheForDev` and `experimental.turbopackFileSystemCacheForBuild`. See [Turbopack FileSystem Caching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/turbopackFileSystemCache) to configure or disable either one. 280 281 ## Async Request APIs (Breaking change) 282 283 Version 15 introduced [Async Request APIs](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-15#async-request-apis-breaking-change) as a breaking change, with **temporary** synchronous compatibility. 284 285 Starting with **Next.js 16**, synchronous access is fully removed. These APIs can only be accessed asynchronously. 286 287 - [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) 288 - [`headers`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) 289 - [`draftMode`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/draft-mode) 290 - `params` in [`layout.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout), [`page.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), [`route.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route), [`default.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/default), [`opengraph-image`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/opengraph-image#opengraph-image), [`twitter-image`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/opengraph-image#twitter-image), [`icon`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/app-icons#icon), and [`apple-icon`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/app-icons#apple-icon). 291 - `searchParams` in [`page.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) 292 293 Use the [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#migrate-to-async-dynamic-apis) to migrate to async Request-time APIs. 294 295 ### Migrating types for async Request-time APIs 296 297 To help migrate to async `params` and `searchParams`, you can run [`npx next typegen`](/docs/app/api-reference/cli/next#next-typegen-options) to automatically generate these globally available types helpers: 298 299 - [`PageProps`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#page-props-helper) 300 - [`LayoutProps`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#layout-props-helper) 301 - [`RouteContext`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route#route-context-helper) 302 303 > **Good to know**: `typegen` was introduced in Next.js 15.5 304 305 This simplifies type-safe migration to the new async API pattern, and enables you to update your components with full type safety, for example: 306 307 ```tsx filename="/app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" 308 export default async function Page(props: PageProps<'/blog/[slug]'>) { 309 const { slug } = await props.params 310 const query = await props.searchParams 311 return

Blog Post: {slug}

312 } 313 ``` 314 315 This approach gives you fully type-safe access to `props.params`, including the `slug`, and to `searchParams`, directly within your page. 316 317 ## Async parameters for icon, and open-graph Image (Breaking change) 318 319 > The props passed to the image generating functions in `opengraph-image`, `twitter-image`, `icon`, and `apple-icon`, are now Promises. 320 321 In previous versions, both the `Image` (image generation function), and the `generateImageMetadata` received a `params` object. The `id` returned by `generateImageMetadata` was passed as a string to the image generation function. 322 323 ```js filename="app/shop/[slug]/opengraph-image.js" 324 // Next.js 15 - synchronous params access 325 export function generateImageMetadata({ params }) { 326 const { slug } = params 327 return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }] 328 } 329 330 // Next.js 15 - synchronous params and id access 331 export default function Image({ params, id }) { 332 const slug = params.slug 333 const imageId = id // string 334 // ... 335 } 336 ``` 337 338 Starting with **Next.js 16**, to align with the [Async Request APIs](#async-request-apis-breaking-change) change, the image generating function now receives `params` and `id` as promises. The `generateImageMetadata` function continues to receive synchronous `params`. 339 340 ```js filename="app/shop/[slug]/opengraph-image.js" 341 export async function generateImageMetadata({ params }) { 342 const { slug } = params 343 return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }] 344 } 345 346 // Next.js 16 - asynchronous params and id access 347 export default async function Image({ params, id }) { 348 const { slug } = await params // params now async 349 const imageId = await id // id is now Promise when using generateImageMetadata 350 // ... 351 } 352 ``` 353 354 ## Async `id` parameter for `sitemap` (Breaking change) 355 356 Previously, the `id` values returned from [`generateSitemaps`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-sitemaps) were passed directly to the `sitemap` generating function. 357 358 ```js filename="app/product/sitemap.js" 359 export async function generateSitemaps() { 360 return [{ id: 0 }, { id: 1 }, { id: 2 }, { id: 3 }] 361 } 362 363 // Next.js 15 - synchronous id access 364 export default async function sitemap({ id }) { 365 const start = id * 50000 // id is a number 366 // ... 367 } 368 ``` 369 370 Starting with **Next.js 16**, the `sitemap` generating function now receives `id` as a promise. 371 372 ```js filename="app/product/sitemap.js" 373 export async function generateSitemaps() { 374 return [{ id: 0 }, { id: 1 }, { id: 2 }, { id: 3 }] 375 } 376 377 // Next.js 16 - asynchronous id access 378 export default async function sitemap({ id }) { 379 const resolvedId = await id // id is now Promise 380 const start = Number(resolvedId) * 50000 381 // ... 382 } 383 ``` 384 385 ## React 19.2 386 387 The App Router in **Next.js 16** uses the latest React [Canary release](https://react.dev/blog/2023/05/03/react-canaries), which includes the newly released React 19.2 features and other features being incrementally stabilized. Highlights include: 388 389 - **[View Transitions](https://react.dev/reference/react/ViewTransition)**: Animate elements that update inside a Transition or navigation 390 - **[`useEffectEvent`](https://react.dev/reference/react/useEffectEvent)**: Extract non-reactive logic from Effects into reusable Effect Event functions 391 - **[Activity](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity)**: Render "background activity" by hiding UI with `display: none` while maintaining state and cleaning up Effects 392 393 Learn more in the [React 19.2 announcement](https://react.dev/blog/2025/10/01/react-19-2). 394 395 ## React Compiler Support 396 397 Built-in support for the React Compiler is now stable in **Next.js 16** following the React Compiler's 1.0 release. The React Compiler automatically memoizes components, reducing unnecessary re-renders with zero manual code changes. 398 399 The `reactCompiler` configuration option has been promoted from `experimental` to stable. It is not enabled by default as we continue gathering build performance data across different application types. 400 401 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 402 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 403 404 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 405 reactCompiler: true, 406 } 407 408 export default nextConfig 409 ``` 410 411 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 412 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 413 const nextConfig = { 414 reactCompiler: true, 415 } 416 417 module.exports = nextConfig 418 ``` 419 420 Install the latest version of the React Compiler plugin: 421 422 ```bash package="pnpm" 423 pnpm add -D babel-plugin-react-compiler 424 ``` 425 426 ```bash package="npm" 427 npm install -D babel-plugin-react-compiler 428 ``` 429 430 ```bash package="yarn" 431 yarn add -D babel-plugin-react-compiler 432 ``` 433 434 ```bash package="bun" 435 bun add -D babel-plugin-react-compiler 436 ``` 437 438 > **Good to know:** Expect compile times in development and during builds to be higher when enabling this option as the React Compiler relies on Babel. 439 440 ## Caching APIs 441 442 ### revalidateTag 443 444 [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) now requires a second argument specifying a [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#reference) profile. The single-argument form is deprecated and will produce a TypeScript error. 445 446 ```ts 447 // Before 448 revalidateTag('posts') 449 450 // After 451 revalidateTag('posts', 'max') 452 ``` 453 454 If you need immediate expiration rather than stale-while-revalidate, use [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) in Server Actions instead. 455 456 ```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 457 'use server' 458 459 import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache' 460 461 export async function updateArticle(articleId: string) { 462 // Mark article data as stale - article readers see stale data while it revalidates 463 revalidateTag(`article-${articleId}`, 'max') 464 } 465 ``` 466 467 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 468 'use server' 469 470 import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache' 471 472 export async function updateArticle(articleId) { 473 // Mark article data as stale - article readers see stale data while it revalidates 474 revalidateTag(`article-${articleId}`, 'max') 475 } 476 ``` 477 478 Use `revalidateTag` for content where a slight delay in updates is acceptable, such as blog posts, product catalogs, or documentation. Users receive stale content while fresh data loads in the background. 479 480 ### updateTag 481 482 [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) is a new [Server Actions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data#what-are-server-functions)-only API that provides **read-your-writes** semantics, where a user makes a change and the UI immediately shows the change, rather than stale data. 483 484 It does this by expiring and immediately refreshing data within the same request. 485 486 ```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 487 'use server' 488 489 import { updateTag } from 'next/cache' 490 491 export async function updateUserProfile(userId: string, profile: Profile) { 492 await db.users.update(userId, profile) 493 494 // Expire cache and refresh immediately - user sees their changes right away 495 updateTag(`user-${userId}`) 496 } 497 ``` 498 499 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 500 'use server' 501 502 import { updateTag } from 'next/cache' 503 504 export async function updateUserProfile(userId, profile) { 505 await db.users.update(userId, profile) 506 507 // Expire cache and refresh immediately - user sees their changes right away 508 updateTag(`user-${userId}`) 509 } 510 ``` 511 512 This ensures interactive features reflect changes immediately. Perfect for forms, user settings, and any workflow where users expect to see their updates instantly. 513 514 Learn more about when to use `updateTag` or `revalidateTag` [here](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag#when-to-use-updatetag). 515 516 ### refresh 517 518 [`refresh`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/refresh) allows you to refresh the client router from within a Server Action. 519 520 ```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 521 'use server' 522 523 import { refresh } from 'next/cache' 524 525 export async function markNotificationAsRead(notificationId: string) { 526 // Update the notification in the database 527 await db.notifications.markAsRead(notificationId) 528 529 // Refresh the notification count displayed in the header 530 refresh() 531 } 532 ``` 533 534 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 535 'use server' 536 537 import { refresh } from 'next/cache' 538 539 export async function markNotificationAsRead(notificationId) { 540 // Update the notification in the database 541 await db.notifications.markAsRead(notificationId) 542 543 // Refresh the notification count displayed in the header 544 refresh() 545 } 546 ``` 547 548 Use it when you need to refresh the client router after performing an action. 549 550 ### cacheLife and cacheTag 551 552 [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) and [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) are now stable. The `unstable_` prefix is no longer needed. 553 554 Wherever you had aliased imports like: 555 556 ```ts 557 import { 558 unstable_cacheLife as cacheLife, 559 unstable_cacheTag as cacheTag, 560 } from 'next/cache' 561 ``` 562 563 You can update your imports to: 564 565 ```ts 566 import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache' 567 ``` 568 569 ## Enhanced Routing and Navigation 570 571 **Next.js 16** includes a complete overhaul of the routing and navigation system, making page transitions leaner and faster. This optimizes how Next.js prefetches and caches navigation data: 572 573 - **Layout deduplication**: When prefetching multiple URLs with a shared layout, the layout is downloaded once. 574 - **Incremental prefetching**: Next.js only prefetches parts not already in cache, rather than entire pages. 575 576 These changes require **no code modifications** and are designed to improve performance across all apps. 577 578 However, you may see more individual prefetch requests with much lower total transfer sizes. We believe this is the right trade-off for nearly all applications. 579 580 If the increased request count causes issues, please let us know by creating an [issue](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues) or [discussion](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions) item. 581 582 ## Partial Prerendering (PPR) 583 584 **Next.js 16** removes the experimental **Partial Prerendering (PPR)** flag and configuration options, including the route level segment `experimental_ppr`. 585 586 Starting with **Next.js 16**, you can opt into PPR using the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) configuration. 587 588 ```js filename="next.config.js" 589 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 590 const nextConfig = { 591 cacheComponents: true, 592 } 593 594 module.exports = nextConfig 595 ``` 596 597 PPR in **Next.js 16** works differently than in **Next.js 15** canaries. If you are using PPR today, stay in the current Next.js 15 canary you are using. See [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components) for migration patterns. 598 599 ```js filename="next.config.js" 600 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 601 const nextConfig = { 602 // If you are using PPR today 603 // stay in the current Next.js 15 canary 604 experimental: { 605 ppr: true, 606 }, 607 } 608 609 module.exports = nextConfig 610 ``` 611 612 ## `middleware` to `proxy` 613 614 The `middleware` filename is deprecated, and has been renamed to `proxy` to clarify network boundary and routing focus. 615 616 The `edge` runtime is **NOT** supported in `proxy`. The `proxy` runtime is `nodejs`, and it cannot be configured. If you want to continue using the `edge` runtime, keep using `middleware`. We will follow up on a minor release with further `edge` runtime instructions. 617 618 ```bash filename="Terminal" 619 # Rename your middleware file 620 mv middleware.ts proxy.ts 621 # or 622 mv middleware.js proxy.js 623 ``` 624 625 The named export `middleware` is also deprecated. Rename your function to `proxy`. 626 627 ```ts filename="proxy.ts" switcher 628 export function proxy(request: Request) {} 629 ``` 630 631 ```js filename="proxy.js" switcher 632 export function proxy(request) {} 633 ``` 634 635 We recommend changing the function name to `proxy`, even if you are using a default export. 636 637 Configuration flags that contained the `middleware` name are also renamed. For example, `skipMiddlewareUrlNormalize` is now `skipProxyUrlNormalize` 638 639 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 640 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 641 642 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 643 skipProxyUrlNormalize: true, 644 } 645 646 export default nextConfig 647 ``` 648 649 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 650 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 651 const nextConfig = { 652 skipProxyUrlNormalize: true, 653 } 654 655 module.exports = nextConfig 656 ``` 657 658 The version 16 [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#160) is able to update these flags too. 659 660 ## `next/image` changes 661 662 ### Local Images with Query Strings (Breaking change) 663 664 Local image sources with query strings now require `images.localPatterns.search` configuration to prevent enumeration attacks. 665 666 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" 667 import Image from 'next/image' 668 669 export default function Page() { 670 return 671 } 672 ``` 673 674 If you need to use query strings with local images, add the pattern to your configuration: 675 676 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 677 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 678 679 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 680 images: { 681 localPatterns: [ 682 { 683 pathname: '/assets/**', 684 search: '?v=1', 685 }, 686 ], 687 }, 688 } 689 690 export default nextConfig 691 ``` 692 693 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 694 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 695 const nextConfig = { 696 images: { 697 localPatterns: [ 698 { 699 pathname: '/assets/**', 700 search: '?v=1', 701 }, 702 ], 703 }, 704 } 705 706 module.exports = nextConfig 707 ``` 708 709 ### `minimumCacheTTL` Default (Breaking change) 710 711 The default value for `images.minimumCacheTTL` has changed from `60 seconds` to `4 hours` (14400 seconds). This reduces revalidation cost for images without cache-control headers. 712 713 For some Next.js users, image revalidation was happening frequently, often because the upstream source images missed a `cache-control` header. This caused revalidation to happen every `60` seconds, which increased CPU usage and cost. 714 715 Since most images do not change often, this short interval is not ideal. Setting the default to 4 hours offers a more durable cache by default, while still allowing images to update a few times per day if needed. 716 717 If you need the previous behavior, change `minimumCacheTTL` to a lower value, for example back to `60` seconds: 718 719 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 720 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 721 722 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 723 images: { 724 minimumCacheTTL: 60, 725 }, 726 } 727 728 export default nextConfig 729 ``` 730 731 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 732 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 733 const nextConfig = { 734 images: { 735 minimumCacheTTL: 60, 736 }, 737 } 738 739 module.exports = nextConfig 740 ``` 741 742 ### `imageSizes` Default (Breaking change) 743 744 The value `16` has been removed from the default `images.imageSizes` array. 745 746 We have looked at request analytics and found out that very few projects ever serve 16 pixels width images. Removing this setting reduces the size of the `srcset` attribute shipped to the browser by `next/image`. 747 748 If you need to support 16px images: 749 750 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 751 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 752 753 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 754 images: { 755 imageSizes: [16, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 256, 384], 756 }, 757 } 758 759 export default nextConfig 760 ``` 761 762 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 763 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 764 const nextConfig = { 765 images: { 766 imageSizes: [16, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 256, 384], 767 }, 768 } 769 770 module.exports = nextConfig 771 ``` 772 773 Rather than lack of developer usage, we believe 16 pixels width images have become less common, because `devicePixelRatio: 2` actually fetches a 32px image to prevent blurriness in retina displays. 774 775 ### `qualities` Default (Breaking change) 776 777 The default value for `images.qualities` has changed from allowing all qualities to only `[75]`. 778 779 If you need to support multiple quality levels: 780 781 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 782 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 783 784 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 785 images: { 786 qualities: [50, 75, 100], 787 }, 788 } 789 790 export default nextConfig 791 ``` 792 793 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 794 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 795 const nextConfig = { 796 images: { 797 qualities: [50, 75, 100], 798 }, 799 } 800 801 module.exports = nextConfig 802 ``` 803 804 If you specify a `quality` prop not included in the `image.qualities` array, the quality will be coerced to the closest value in `images.qualities`. For example, given the configuration above, a `quality` prop of 80, is coerced to 75. 805 806 ### Local IP Restriction (Breaking change) 807 808 A new security restriction blocks local IP optimization by default. Set `images.dangerouslyAllowLocalIP` to `true` only for private networks. 809 810 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 811 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 812 813 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 814 images: { 815 dangerouslyAllowLocalIP: true, // Only for private networks 816 }, 817 } 818 819 export default nextConfig 820 ``` 821 822 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 823 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 824 const nextConfig = { 825 images: { 826 dangerouslyAllowLocalIP: true, // Only for private networks 827 }, 828 } 829 830 module.exports = nextConfig 831 ``` 832 833 This might be necessary when hosting Next.js in a VPC with split-horizon DNS and you receive status 400 Bad Request. Only enable once you understand the SSRF risk. 834 835 ### Maximum Redirects (Breaking change) 836 837 The default for `images.maximumRedirects` has changed from unlimited to 3 redirects maximum. 838 839 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 840 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 841 842 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 843 images: { 844 maximumRedirects: 0, // Disable redirects 845 // or 846 maximumRedirects: 5, // Increase for edge cases 847 }, 848 } 849 850 export default nextConfig 851 ``` 852 853 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 854 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 855 const nextConfig = { 856 images: { 857 maximumRedirects: 0, // Disable redirects 858 // or 859 maximumRedirects: 5, // Increase for edge cases 860 }, 861 } 862 863 module.exports = nextConfig 864 ``` 865 866 ### `next/legacy/image` Component (deprecated) 867 868 The `next/legacy/image` component is deprecated. Use `next/image` instead: 869 870 ```tsx 871 // Before 872 import Image from 'next/legacy/image' 873 874 // After 875 import Image from 'next/image' 876 ``` 877 878 ### `images.domains` Configuration (deprecated) 879 880 The `images.domains` config is deprecated. 881 882 ```js filename="next.config.js" 883 // image.domains is deprecated 884 module.exports = { 885 images: { 886 domains: ['example.com'], 887 }, 888 } 889 ``` 890 891 Use `images.remotePatterns` instead for improved security: 892 893 ```js filename="next.config.js" 894 // Use image.remotePatterns instead 895 module.exports = { 896 images: { 897 remotePatterns: [ 898 { 899 protocol: 'https', 900 hostname: 'example.com', 901 }, 902 ], 903 }, 904 } 905 ``` 906 907 ## Concurrent `dev` and `build` 908 909 `next dev` and `next build` now use separate output directories, enabling concurrent execution. The `next dev` command outputs to `.next/dev`. 910 911 Additionally, a lockfile mechanism prevents multiple `next dev` or `next build` instances on the same project. 912 913 The [Turbopack tracing command](/docs/app/guides/local-development#turbopack-tracing) should be: 914 915 ```bash package="pnpm" 916 pnpm next internal trace .next-profiles/trace-turbopack.bin 917 ``` 918 919 ```bash package="npm" 920 npx next internal trace .next-profiles/trace-turbopack.bin 921 ``` 922 923 ```bash package="yarn" 924 yarn next internal trace .next-profiles/trace-turbopack.bin 925 ``` 926 927 ```bash package="bun" 928 bunx next internal trace .next-profiles/trace-turbopack.bin 929 ``` 930 931 ## Parallel Routes `default.js` requirement 932 933 All [parallel route](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/parallel-routes) slots now require explicit `default.js` files. Builds will fail without them. 934 935 To maintain previous behavior, create a [`default.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/default) file that calls `notFound()` or returns `null`. 936 937 ```tsx filename="app/@modal/default.tsx" 938 import { notFound } from 'next/navigation' 939 940 export default function Default() { 941 notFound() 942 } 943 ``` 944 945 Or return `null`: 946 947 ```tsx filename="app/@modal/default.tsx" 948 export default function Default() { 949 return null 950 } 951 ``` 952 953 ## ESLint Flat Config 954 955 `@next/eslint-plugin-next` now defaults to ESLint Flat Config format, aligning with ESLint v10 which will drop legacy config support. 956 957 Make sure to review our API reference for the [`@next/eslint-plugin-next`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/eslint#setup-eslint) plugin. 958 959 If you're using the legacy `.eslintrc` format, consider migrating to the flat config format. See the [ESLint migration guide](https://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/configure/migration-guide) for details. 960 961 ## Scroll Behavior Override 962 963 In **previous versions of Next.js**, if you had set `scroll-behavior: smooth` globally on your `` element via CSS, Next.js would override this during SPA route transitions, as follows: 964 965 1. Temporarily set `scroll-behavior` to `auto` 966 2. Perform the navigation (causing instant scroll to top) 967 3. Restore your original `scroll-behavior` value 968 969 This ensured that page navigation always felt snappy and instant, even when you had smooth scrolling enabled for in-page navigation. However, this manipulation could be expensive, especially at the start of every navigation. 970 971 In **Next.js 16**, this behavior has changed. By default, Next.js will **no longer override** your `scroll-behavior` setting during navigation. 972 973 **If you want Next.js to perform this override** (the previous default behavior), add the `data-scroll-behavior="smooth"` attribute to your `` element: 974 975 ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" 976 export default function RootLayout({ children }) { 977 return ( 978 979 {children} 980 981 ) 982 } 983 ``` 984 985 ## Performance Improvements 986 987 Significant performance optimizations for `next dev` and `next start` commands, along with improved terminal output with clearer formatting, better error messages, and improved performance metrics. 988 989 **Next.js 16** removes the `size` and `First Load JS` metrics from the `next build` output. We found these to be inaccurate in server-driven architectures using React Server Components. Both our Turbopack and Webpack implementations had issues, and disagreed on how to account for Client Components payload. 990 991 The most effective way to measure actual route performance is through tools such as [Chrome Lighthouse](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/overview) or Vercel Analytics, which focus on Core Web Vitals and downloaded resource sizes. 992 993 ### `next dev` config load 994 995 In previous versions the Next config file was loaded twice during development: 996 997 - When running the `next dev` command 998 - When the `next dev` command started the Next.js server 999 1000 This was inefficient because the `next dev` command doesn't need the config file to start the Next.js server. 1001 1002 A consequence of this change is that, when running `next dev` checking if `process.argv` includes `'dev'`, in your Next.js config file, will return `false`. 1003 1004 > **Good to know**: The `typegen`, and `build` commands, are still visible in `process.argv`. 1005 1006 This is specially important for plugins that trigger side-effects on `next dev`. If that's the case, it might be enough to check if `NODE_ENV` is set to `development`. 1007 1008 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1009 import { startServer } from 'docs-lib/dev-server' 1010 1011 const isDev = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development' 1012 1013 if (isDev) { 1014 startServer() 1015 } 1016 1017 const nextConfig = { 1018 /* Your config options */ 1019 } 1020 1021 module.exports = nextConfig 1022 ``` 1023 1024 Alternatively, use the [`phase`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js#phase) in which the configuration is loaded. 1025 1026 ## Build Adapters API (alpha) 1027 1028 Following the [Build Adapters RFC](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/77740), the first alpha version of the Build Adapters API is now available. 1029 1030 Build Adapters allow you to create custom adapters that hook into the build process, enabling deployment platforms and custom build integrations to modify Next.js configuration or process build output. 1031 1032 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1033 const nextConfig = { 1034 experimental: { 1035 adapterPath: require.resolve('./my-adapter.js'), 1036 }, 1037 } 1038 1039 module.exports = nextConfig 1040 ``` 1041 1042 `adapterPath` was promoted to a stable, top-level option in 16.2.0. See [`adapterPath`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/adapterPath) for the current API reference. 1043 1044 ## Modern Sass API 1045 1046 `sass-loader` has been bumped to v16, which supports [modern Sass syntax](https://sass-lang.com/documentation/js-api/#md:usage) and new features. 1047 1048 ## Removals 1049 1050 These features were previously deprecated and are now removed: 1051 1052 ### AMP Support 1053 1054 AMP adoption has declined significantly, and maintaining this feature adds complexity to the framework. All AMP APIs and configurations have been removed: 1055 1056 - `amp` configuration from your Next config file 1057 - `next/amp` hook imports and usage (`useAmp`) 1058 1059 ```tsx 1060 // Removed 1061 import { useAmp } from 'next/amp' 1062 1063 // Removed 1064 export const config = { amp: true } 1065 ``` 1066 1067 - `export const config = { amp: true }` from pages 1068 1069 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1070 const nextConfig = { 1071 // Removed 1072 amp: { 1073 canonicalBase: 'https://example.com', 1074 }, 1075 } 1076 1077 module.exports = nextConfig 1078 ``` 1079 1080 Evaluate if AMP is still necessary for your use case. Most performance benefits can now be achieved through Next.js's built-in optimizations and modern web standards. 1081 1082 ### `next lint` Command 1083 1084 The `next lint` command has been removed. Use Biome or ESLint directly. `next build` no longer runs linting. 1085 1086 A codemod is available to automate migration: 1087 1088 ```bash package="pnpm" 1089 pnpm dlx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli . 1090 ``` 1091 1092 ```bash package="npm" 1093 npx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli . 1094 ``` 1095 1096 ```bash package="yarn" 1097 yarn dlx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli . 1098 ``` 1099 1100 ```bash package="bun" 1101 bunx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli . 1102 ``` 1103 1104 The `eslint` option in the Next.js config file is also removed. 1105 1106 ```js filename="next.config.mjs" 1107 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 1108 const nextConfig = { 1109 // No longer supported 1110 // eslint: {}, 1111 } 1112 1113 export default nextConfig 1114 ``` 1115 1116 ### Runtime Configuration 1117 1118 `serverRuntimeConfig` and `publicRuntimeConfig` have been removed. Use environment variables instead. 1119 1120 **Before (Next.js 15):** 1121 1122 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1123 module.exports = { 1124 serverRuntimeConfig: { 1125 dbUrl: process.env.DATABASE_URL, 1126 }, 1127 publicRuntimeConfig: { 1128 apiUrl: '/api', 1129 }, 1130 } 1131 ``` 1132 1133 ```tsx filename="pages/index.tsx" 1134 import getConfig from 'next/config' 1135 1136 export default function Page() { 1137 const { publicRuntimeConfig } = getConfig() 1138 return

API URL: {publicRuntimeConfig.apiUrl}

1139 } 1140 ``` 1141 1142 **After (Next.js 16):** 1143 1144 For server-only values, access environment variables directly in Server Components: 1145 1146 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" 1147 async function fetchData() { 1148 const dbUrl = process.env.DATABASE_URL 1149 // Use for server-side operations only 1150 return await db.query(dbUrl, 'SELECT * FROM users') 1151 } 1152 1153 export default async function Page() { 1154 const data = await fetchData() 1155 return
{/* render data */}
1156 } 1157 ``` 1158 1159 > **Good to know**: Use the [taint API](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/taint) to prevent accidentally passing sensitive server values to Client Components. 1160 1161 For client-accessible values, use the `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix: 1162 1163 ```bash filename=".env.local" 1164 NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL="/api" 1165 ``` 1166 1167 ```tsx filename="app/components/client-component.tsx" 1168 'use client' 1169 1170 export default function ClientComponent() { 1171 const apiUrl = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL 1172 return

API URL: {apiUrl}

1173 } 1174 ``` 1175 1176 To ensure environment variables are read at runtime (not bundled at build time), use the [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection) function before reading from `process.env`: 1177 1178 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" 1179 import { connection } from 'next/server' 1180 1181 export default async function Page() { 1182 await connection() 1183 const config = process.env.RUNTIME_CONFIG 1184 return

{config}

1185 } 1186 ``` 1187 1188 Learn more about [environment variables](/docs/app/guides/environment-variables). 1189 1190 ### `devIndicators` Options 1191 1192 The following options have been removed from [`devIndicators`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/devIndicators): 1193 1194 - `appIsrStatus` 1195 - `buildActivity` 1196 - `buildActivityPosition` 1197 1198 The indicator itself remains available. 1199 1200 ### `experimental.dynamicIO` and `experimental.useCache` 1201 1202 The `experimental.dynamicIO` and `experimental.useCache` flags have been removed. 1203 1204 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1205 // Before: experimental.useCache 1206 module.exports = { 1207 experimental: { 1208 useCache: true, 1209 }, 1210 } 1211 ``` 1212 1213 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1214 // Before: experimental.dynamicIO 1215 module.exports = { 1216 experimental: { 1217 dynamicIO: true, 1218 }, 1219 } 1220 ``` 1221 1222 If you were actively using these flags, migrate to top-level [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents): 1223 1224 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 1225 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 1226 1227 // After 1228 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 1229 cacheComponents: true, 1230 } 1231 1232 export default nextConfig 1233 ``` 1234 1235 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 1236 // After 1237 module.exports = { 1238 cacheComponents: true, 1239 } 1240 ``` 1241 1242 If you were not actively adopting Cache Components, remove the flags instead. Enabling `cacheComponents` is not a rename-only change: it can surface build errors for uncached data outside of `` and requires adopting the Cache Components model. 1243 1244 For the full migration path, see [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components). 1245 1246 ### `unstable_rootParams` 1247 1248 The `unstable_rootParams` function has been removed. Use [`next/root-params`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-root-params) instead. 1249

2	title: dynamicParams
3	description: API reference for the dynamicParams route segment config option.
4	---
5	
6	The `dynamicParams` option allows you to control what happens when a dynamic segment is visited that was not generated with [generateStaticParams](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params).
7	
8	```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx" switcher
9	export const dynamicParams = true // true | false
10	```
11	
12	```js filename="layout.js | page.js | route.js" switcher
13	export const dynamicParams = true // true | false
14	```
15	
16	- **`true`** (default): Dynamic route segments not included in `generateStaticParams` are generated at request time.
17	- **`false`**: Dynamic route segments not included in `generateStaticParams` will return a 404.
18	
19	> **Good to know**:
20	>
21	> - This option replaces the `fallback: true | false | blocking` option of `getStaticPaths` in the `pages` directory.
22	> - `dynamicParams` is not available when [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.

1 --- 2 title: route.js 3 description: API reference for the route.js special file. 4 --- 5 6 Route Handlers allow you to create custom request handlers for a given route using the Web [Request](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request) and [Response](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Response) APIs. 7 8 ```ts filename="route.ts" switcher 9 export async function GET() { 10 return Response.json({ message: 'Hello World' }) 11 } 12 ``` 13 14 ```js filename="route.js" switcher 15 export async function GET() { 16 return Response.json({ message: 'Hello World' }) 17 } 18 ``` 19 20 ## Reference 21 22 ### HTTP Methods 23 24 A **route** file allows you to create custom request handlers for a given route. The following [HTTP methods](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods) are supported: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `HEAD`, and `OPTIONS`. 25 26 ```ts filename="route.ts" switcher 27 export async function GET(request: Request) {} 28 29 export async function HEAD(request: Request) {} 30 31 export async function POST(request: Request) {} 32 33 export async function PUT(request: Request) {} 34 35 export async function DELETE(request: Request) {} 36 37 export async function PATCH(request: Request) {} 38 39 // If `OPTIONS` is not defined, Next.js will automatically implement `OPTIONS` and set the appropriate Response `Allow` header depending on the other methods defined in the Route Handler. 40 export async function OPTIONS(request: Request) {} 41 ``` 42 43 ```js filename="route.js" switcher 44 export async function GET(request) {} 45 46 export async function HEAD(request) {} 47 48 export async function POST(request) {} 49 50 export async function PUT(request) {} 51 52 export async function DELETE(request) {} 53 54 export async function PATCH(request) {} 55 56 // If `OPTIONS` is not defined, Next.js will automatically implement `OPTIONS` and set the appropriate Response `Allow` header depending on the other methods defined in the Route Handler. 57 export async function OPTIONS(request) {} 58 ``` 59 60 ### Parameters 61 62 #### `request` (optional) 63 64 The `request` object is a [NextRequest](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-request) object, which is an extension of the Web [Request](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request) API. `NextRequest` gives you further control over the incoming request, including easily accessing `cookies` and an extended, parsed, URL object `nextUrl`. 65 66 ```ts filename="route.ts" switcher 67 import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server' 68 69 export async function GET(request: NextRequest) { 70 const url = request.nextUrl 71 } 72 ``` 73 74 ```js filename="route.js" switcher 75 export async function GET(request) { 76 const url = request.nextUrl 77 } 78 ``` 79 80 #### `context` (optional) 81 82 - **`params`**: a promise that resolves to an object containing the [dynamic route parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) for the current route. 83 84 ```ts filename="app/dashboard/[team]/route.ts" switcher 85 export async function GET( 86 request: Request, 87 { params }: { params: Promise<{ team: string }> } 88 ) { 89 const { team } = await params 90 } 91 ``` 92 93 ```js filename="app/dashboard/[team]/route.js" switcher 94 export async function GET(request, { params }) { 95 const { team } = await params 96 } 97 ``` 98 99 | Example | URL | `params` | 100 | -------------------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------- | 101 | `app/dashboard/[team]/route.js` | `/dashboard/1` | `Promise<{ team: '1' }>` | 102 | `app/shop/[tag]/[item]/route.js` | `/shop/1/2` | `Promise<{ tag: '1', item: '2' }>` | 103 | `app/blog/[...slug]/route.js` | `/blog/1/2` | `Promise<{ slug: ['1', '2'] }>` | 104 105 ### Route Context Helper 106 107 You can type the Route Handler context using `RouteContext` to get strongly typed `params` from a route literal. `RouteContext` is a globally available helper. 108 109 ```ts filename="app/users/[id]/route.ts" 110 import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server' 111 112 export async function GET(_req: NextRequest, ctx: RouteContext<'/users/[id]'>) { 113 const { id } = await ctx.params 114 return Response.json({ id }) 115 } 116 ``` 117 118 > **Good to know** 119 > 120 > - Types are generated during `next dev`, `next build` or `next typegen`. 121 > - After type generation, the `RouteContext` helper is globally available. It doesn't need to be imported. 122 123 ## Examples 124 125 ### Cookies 126 127 You can read or set cookies with [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) from `next/headers`. 128 129 ```ts filename="route.ts" switcher 130 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 131 132 export async function GET(request: NextRequest) { 133 const cookieStore = await cookies() 134 135 const a = cookieStore.get('a') 136 const b = cookieStore.set('b', '1') 137 const c = cookieStore.delete('c') 138 } 139 ``` 140 141 ```js filename="route.js" switcher 142 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 143 144 export async function GET(request) { 145 const cookieStore = await cookies() 146 147 const a = cookieStore.get('a') 148 const b = cookieStore.set('b', '1') 149 const c = cookieStore.delete('c') 150 } 151 ``` 152 153 Alternatively, you can return a new `Response` using the [`Set-Cookie`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Set-Cookie) header. 154 155 ```ts filename="app/api/route.ts" switcher 156 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 157 158 export async function GET(request: Request) { 159 const cookieStore = await cookies() 160 const token = cookieStore.get('token') 161 162 return new Response('Hello, Next.js!', { 163 status: 200, 164 headers: { 'Set-Cookie': `token=${token.value}` }, 165 }) 166 } 167 ``` 168 169 ```js filename="app/api/route.js" switcher 170 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 171 172 export async function GET(request) { 173 const cookieStore = await cookies() 174 const token = cookieStore.get('token') 175 176 return new Response('Hello, Next.js!', { 177 status: 200, 178 headers: { 'Set-Cookie': `token=${token.value}` }, 179 }) 180 } 181 ``` 182 183 You can also use the underlying Web APIs to read cookies from the request ([`NextRequest`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-request)): 184 185 ```ts filename="app/api/route.ts" switcher 186 import { type NextRequest } from 'next/server' 187 188 export async function GET(request: NextRequest) { 189 const token = request.cookies.get('token') 190 } 191 ``` 192 193 ```js filename="app/api/route.js" switcher 194 export async function GET(request) { 195 const token = request.cookies.get('token') 196 } 197 ``` 198 199 ### Headers 200 201 You can read headers with [`headers`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) from `next/headers`. 202 203 ```ts filename="route.ts" switcher 204 import { headers } from 'next/headers' 205 import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server' 206 207 export async function GET(request: NextRequest) { 208 const headersList = await headers() 209 const referer = headersList.get('referer') 210 } 211 ``` 212 213 ```js filename="route.js" switcher 214 import { headers } from 'next/headers' 215 216 export async function GET(request) { 217 const headersList = await headers() 218 const referer = headersList.get('referer') 219 } 220 ``` 221 222 This `headers` instance is read-only. To set headers, you need to return a new `Response` with new `headers`. 223 224 ```ts filename="app/api/route.ts" switcher 225 import { headers } from 'next/headers' 226 227 export async function GET(request: Request) { 228 const headersList = await headers() 229 const referer = headersList.get('referer') 230 231 return new Response('Hello, Next.js!', { 232 status: 200, 233 headers: { referer: referer }, 234 }) 235 } 236 ``` 237 238 ```js filename="app/api/route.js" switcher 239 import { headers } from 'next/headers' 240 241 export async function GET(request) { 242 const headersList = await headers() 243 const referer = headersList.get('referer') 244 245 return new Response('Hello, Next.js!', { 246 status: 200, 247 headers: { referer: referer }, 248 }) 249 } 250 ``` 251 252 You can also use the underlying Web APIs to read headers from the request ([`NextRequest`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-request)): 253 254 ```ts filename="app/api/route.ts" switcher 255 import { type 1 --- 2 title: not-found.js 3 description: API reference for the not-found.js file. 4 --- 5 6 Next.js provides two conventions to handle not found cases: 7 8 - **`not-found.js`**: Used when you call the [`notFound`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) function in a route segment. 9 - **`global-not-found.js`**: Used to define a global 404 page for unmatched routes across your entire app. This is handled at the routing level and doesn't depend on rendering a layout or page. 10 11 ## `not-found.js` 12 13 The **not-found** file is used to render UI when the [`notFound`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) function is thrown within a route segment. Along with serving a custom UI, Next.js will return a `200` HTTP status code for streamed responses, and `404` for non-streamed responses (see [Status Codes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading#status-codes) for details about SEO). 14 15 ```tsx filename="app/not-found.tsx" switcher 16 import Link from 'next/link' 17 18 export default function NotFound() { 19 return ( 20
21

Not Found

22

Could not find requested resource

23 Return Home 24
25 ) 26 } 27 ``` 28 29 ```jsx filename="app/blog/not-found.js" switcher 30 import Link from 'next/link' 31 32 export default function NotFound() { 33 return ( 34
35

Not Found

36

Could not find requested resource

37 Return Home 38
39 ) 40 } 41 ``` 42 43 In the [component hierarchy](/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure#component-hierarchy), `not-found.js` renders between `loading.js` and `page.js`. It is wrapped by the `` boundary from `loading.js` and the error boundary from `error.js` in the same segment. 44 45 > **Good to know**: The default not found UI follows the operating system's color scheme via `prefers-color-scheme` and does not read an app-level theme (such as a class or `data-theme` attribute on ``). Because it renders inside your root layout, the quickest way to match an explicit theme is to add a higher-specificity rule pair in your global stylesheet, scoped to your theme selector — for example `html[data-theme='light'] body` and `html[data-theme='dark'] body`. For full control over the markup, provide your own `not-found.js`. 46 47 ## `global-not-found.js` (experimental) 48 49 The `global-not-found.js` file lets you define a 404 page for your entire application. Unlike `not-found.js`, which works at the route level, this is used when a requested URL doesn't match any route at all. During rendering, `children` will be populated with the route segments the layout is wrapping. 3	description: Learn how to add Metadata to your Next.js application for improved search engine optimization (SEO) and web shareability.

11	    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents
12	---
13	
14	You can use the `metadata` object or the `generateMetadata` function to define metadata.
15	
16	## The `metadata` object
17	
18	To define static metadata, export a [`Metadata` object](#metadata-fields) from a `layout.js` or `page.js` file.
19	
20	```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx" switcher
21	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
22	
23	export const metadata: Metadata = {
24	  title: '...',
25	  description: '...',
26	}
27	
28	export default function Page() {}
29	```
30	
31	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js" switcher
32	export const metadata = {
33	  title: '...',
34	  description: '...',
35	}
36	
37	export default function Page() {}
38	```
39	
40	> See the [Metadata Fields](#metadata-fields) for a complete list of supported options.
41	
42	## `generateMetadata` function
43	
44	Dynamic metadata depends on **dynamic information**, such as the current route parameters, external data, or `metadata` in parent segments, can be set by exporting a `generateMetadata` function that returns a [`Metadata` object](#metadata-fields).
45	
46	Resolving `generateMetadata` is part of rendering the page. If the page can be prerendered and `generateMetadata` doesn't introduce dynamic behavior, the resulting metadata is included in the page's initial HTML.
47	
48	Otherwise the metadata resolved from `generateMetadata` [can be streamed](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#streaming-metadata) after sending the initial UI.
49	
50	```tsx filename="app/products/[id]/page.tsx" switcher
51	import type { Metadata, ResolvingMetadata } from 'next'
52	
53	type Props = {
54	  params: Promise<{ id: string }>
55	  searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }>
56	}
57	
58	export async function generateMetadata(
59	  { params, searchParams }: Props,
60	  parent: ResolvingMetadata
61	): Promise<Metadata> {
62	  // read route params
63	  const { id } = await params
64	
65	  // fetch data
66	  const product = await fetch(`https://.../${id}`).then((res) => res.json())
67	
68	  // optionally access and extend (rather than replace) parent metadata
69	  const previousImages = (await parent).openGraph?.images || []
70	
71	  return {
72	    title: product.title,
73	    openGraph: {
74	      images: ['/some-specific-page-image.jpg', ...previousImages],
75	    },
76	  }
77	}
78	
79	export default function Page({ params, searchParams }: Props) {}
80	```
81	
82	```jsx filename="app/products/[id]/page.js" switcher

84	  // read route params
85	  const { id } = await params
86	
87	  // fetch data
88	  const product = await fetch(`https://.../${id}`).then((res) => res.json())
89	
90	  // optionally access and extend (rather than replace) parent metadata
91	  const previousImages = (await parent).openGraph?.images || []
92	
93	  return {
94	    title: product.title,
95	    openGraph: {
96	      images: ['/some-specific-page-image.jpg', ...previousImages],
97	    },
98	  }
99	}
100	
101	export default function Page({ params, searchParams }) {}
102	```
103	
104	For type completion of `params` and `searchParams`, you can type the first argument with [`PageProps<'/route'>`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#page-props-helper) or [`LayoutProps<'/route'>`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#layout-props-helper) for pages and layouts respectively.
105	
106	> **Good to know**:
107	>
108	> - Metadata can be added to `layout.js` and `page.js` files.
109	> - Next.js will automatically resolve the metadata, and create the relevant `<head>` tags for the page.
110	> - The `metadata` object and `generateMetadata` function exports are **only supported in Server Components**.
111	> - You cannot export both the `metadata` object and `generateMetadata` function from the same route segment.
112	> - `fetch` requests inside `generateMetadata` are automatically [memoized](/docs/app/glossary#memoization) for the same data across `generateMetadata`, `generateStaticParams`, Layouts, Pages, and Server Components.
113	> - React [`cache` can be used](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) if `fetch` is unavailable.
114	> - [File-based metadata](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata) has the higher priority and will override the `metadata` object and `generateMetadata` function.
115	
116	## Why `generateMetadata` is Server Component only
117	
118	`generateMetadata` and the `metadata` export are only supported in Server Components because metadata must be resolved on the server before the page component is rendered. This allows Next.js to include the metadata in the initial HTML response.
119	
120	If you need to use Client Component features, keep your `page.tsx` as a Server Component and move the Client Component logic to a separate file:
121	
122	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
123	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
124	import { InteractiveComponent } from './interactive-component'
125	
126	export const metadata: Metadata = {
127	  title: 'My Page',
128	}
129	
130	export default function Page() {
131	  return <InteractiveComponent />
132	}
133	```
134	
135	```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher
136	import { InteractiveComponent } from './interactive-component'
137	
138	export const metadata = {
139	  title: 'My Page',
140	}
141	
142	export default function Page() {
143	  return <InteractiveComponent />
144	}
145	```
146	
147	```tsx filename="app/interactive-component.tsx" switcher

149	
150	export function InteractiveComponent() {
151	  // Client-side interactivity (hooks, event handlers, etc.)
152	}
153	```
154	
155	```jsx filename="app/interactive-component.js" switcher
156	'use client'
157	
158	export function InteractiveComponent() {
159	  // Client-side interactivity (hooks, event handlers, etc.)
160	}
161	```
162	
163	## Reference
164	
165	### Parameters
166	
167	`generateMetadata` function accepts the following parameters:
168	
169	- `props` - An object containing the parameters of the current route:
170	  - `params` - An object containing the [dynamic route parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) object from the root segment down to the segment `generateMetadata` is called from. Examples:
171	
172	    | Route                           | URL         | `params`                  |
173	    | ------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------- |
174	    | `app/shop/[slug]/page.js`       | `/shop/1`   | `{ slug: '1' }`           |
175	    | `app/shop/[tag]/[item]/page.js` | `/shop/1/2` | `{ tag: '1', item: '2' }` |
176	    | `app/shop/[...slug]/page.js`    | `/shop/1/2` | `{ slug: ['1', '2'] }`    |
177	
178	  - `searchParams` - An object containing the current URL's [search params](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Learn/Common_questions/What_is_a_URL#parameters). Examples:
179	
180	    | URL             | `searchParams`       |
181	    | --------------- | -------------------- |
182	    | `/shop?a=1`     | `{ a: '1' }`         |
183	    | `/shop?a=1&b=2` | `{ a: '1', b: '2' }` |
184	    | `/shop?a=1&a=2` | `{ a: ['1', '2'] }`  |
185	
186	- `parent` - A promise of the resolved metadata from parent route segments.
187	
188	### Returns
189	
190	`generateMetadata` should return a [`Metadata` object](#metadata-fields) containing one or more metadata fields.
191	
192	> **Good to know**:
193	>
194	> - If metadata doesn't depend on request information, it should be defined using the static [`metadata` object](#the-metadata-object) rather than `generateMetadata`.
195	> - `fetch` requests are automatically memoized for the same data across `generateMetadata`, `generateStaticParams`, Layouts, Pages, and Server Components. React [`cache` can be used](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) if `fetch` is unavailable.
196	> - `searchParams` are only available in `page.js` segments.
197	> - The [`redirect()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/redirect) and [`notFound()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) Next.js methods can also be used inside `generateMetadata`.
198	
199	### Metadata Fields
200	
201	The following fields are supported:
202	
203	#### `title`
204	
205	The `title` attribute is used to set the title of the document. It can be defined as a simple [string](#string) or an optional [template object](#template).
206	
207	##### String
208	
209	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js"
210	export const metadata = {
211	  title: 'Next.js',
212	}
213	```
214	
215	```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
216	<title>Next.js</title>
217	```
218	
219	##### `default`
220	
221	`title.default` can be used to provide a **fallback title** to child route segments that don't define a `title`.
222	
223	```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx"
224	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
225	
226	export const metadata: Metadata = {
227	  title: {
228	    default: 'Acme',
229	  },
230	}
231	```
232	
233	```tsx filename="app/about/page.tsx"
234	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
235	
236	export const metadata: Metadata = {}
237	
238	// Output: <title>Acme</title>
239	```
240	
241	##### `template`
242	
243	`title.template` can be used to add a prefix or a suffix to `titles` defined in **child** route segments.
244	
245	```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher
246	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
247	
248	export const metadata: Metadata = {
249	  title: {
250	    template: '%s | Acme',
251	    default: 'Acme', // a default is required when creating a template
252	  },
253	}
254	```
255	
256	```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher
257	export const metadata = {
258	  title: {
259	    template: '%s | Acme',
260	    default: 'Acme', // a default is required when creating a template
261	  },
262	}
263	```
264	
265	```tsx filename="app/about/page.tsx" switcher
266	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
267	
268	export const metadata: Metadata = {
269	  title: 'About',
270	}
271	
272	// Output: <title>About | Acme</title>
273	```
274	
275	```jsx filename="app/about/page.js" switcher
276	export const metadata = {
277	  title: 'About',
278	}
279	
280	// Output: <title>About | Acme</title>
281	```
282	
283	> **Good to know**:
284	>
285	> - `title.template` applies to **child** route segments and **not** the segment it's defined in. This means:
286	>   - `title.default` is **required** when you add a `title.template`.
287	>   - `title.template` defined in `layout.js` will not apply to a `title` defined in a `page.js` of the same route segment.
288	>   - `title.template` defined in `page.js` has no effect because a page is always the terminating segment (it doesn't have any children route segments).
289	> - `title.template` has **no effect** if a route has not defined a `title` or `title.default`.
290

292	
293	`title.absolute` can be used to provide a title that **ignores** `title.template` set in parent segments.
294	
295	```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher

297	
298	export const metadata: Metadata = {
299	  title: {
300	    template: '%s | Acme',
301	  },
302	}
303	```
304	
305	```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher
306	export const metadata = {
307	  title: {
308	    template: '%s | Acme',
309	  },
310	}
311	```
312	
313	```tsx filename="app/about/page.tsx" switcher
314	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
315	
316	export const metadata: Metadata = {
317	  title: {
318	    absolute: 'About',
319	  },
320	}
321	
322	// Output: <title>About</title>
323	```
324	
325	```jsx filename="app/about/page.js" switcher
326	export const metadata = {
327	  title: {
328	    absolute: 'About',
329	  },
330	}

title: useRouter
description: API reference for the useRouter hook.
---

The `useRouter` hook allows you to programmatically change routes inside [Client Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components).

> **Recommendation:** Use the [`<Link>` component](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link) for navigation unless you have a specific requirement for using `useRouter`.

```tsx filename="app/example-client-component.tsx" switcher
'use client'

import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'

export default function Page() {
  const router = useRouter()

  return (
    <button type="button" onClick={() => router.push('/dashboard')}>
      Dashboard
    </button>
  )
}
```

```jsx filename="app/example-client-component.js" switcher
'use client'

import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'

export default function Page() {
  const router = useRouter()

  return (
    <button type="button" onClick={() => router.push('/dashboard')}>
      Dashboard
    </button>
  )
}
```

## `useRouter()`

- `router.push(href: string, { scroll: boolean, transitionTypes: string[] })`: Perform a client-side navigation to the provided route. Adds a new entry into the [browser's history stack](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/History_API). The optional `transitionTypes` are passed to [`React.addTransitionType`](https://react.dev/reference/react/addTransitionType) inside the navigation Transition.
- `router.replace(href: string, { scroll: boolean, transitionTypes: string[] })`: Perform a client-side navigation to the provided route without adding a new entry into the browser’s history stack. The optional `transitionTypes` are passed to [`React.addTransitionType`](https://react.dev/reference/react/addTransitionType) inside the navigation Transition.
- `router.refresh()`: Refresh the current route. Making a new request to the server, re-fetching data requests, and re-rendering Server Components. The client will merge the updated React Server Component payload without losing unaffected client-side React (e.g. `useState`) or browser state (e.g. scroll position). This clears the [Client Cache](/docs/app/glossary#client-cache) for the current route, but does **not** invalidate the server-side cache. Use [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath) or [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) to invalidate server-side cached data.
- `router.prefetch(href: string, options?: { onInvalidate?: () => void })`: [Prefetch](/docs/app/getting-started/linking-and-navigating#prefetching) the provided route for faster client-side transitions. The optional `onInvalidate` callback is called when the [prefetched data becomes stale](/docs/app/guides/prefetching#extending-or-ejecting-link).
- `router.back()`: Navigate back to the previous route in the browser’s history stack.
- `router.forward()`: Navigate forwards to the next page in the browser’s history stack.
- `router.bfcacheId`: An opaque string identifier scoped to the current route segment. It changes when the surrounding segment is freshly created by a push or replace navigation, and stays the same for back/forward navigations, `router.refresh()`, and search-param- or hash-only navigations. See [`bfcacheId`](#bfcacheid) below for details.

> **Good to know**:
>
> - You must not send untrusted or unsanitized URLs to `router.push` or `router.replace`, as this can open your site to cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities. For example, `javascript:` URLs sent to `router.push` or `router.replace` will be executed in the context of your page.
> - The `<Link>` component automatically prefetch routes as they become visible in the viewport.
> - `refresh()` could re-produce the same result if fetch requests are cached. Other Request-time APIs like `cookies` and `headers` could also change the response.
> - The `onInvalidate` callback is called at most once per prefetch request. It signals when you may want to trigger a new prefetch for updated route data.

### Migrating from `next/router`

- The `useRouter` hook should be imported from `next/navigation` and not `next/router` when using the App Router
- The `pathname` string has been removed and is replaced by [`usePathname()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-pathname)
- The `query` object has been removed and is replaced by [`useSearchParams()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-search-params)
- `router.events` has been replaced. [See below.](#router-events)

[View the full migration guide](/docs/app/guides/migrating/app-router-migration).

## Examples

### Router events

You can listen for page changes by composing other Client Component hooks like `usePathname` and `useSearchParams`.

```jsx filename="app/components/navigation-events.js"
'use client'

import { useEffect } from 'react'
import { usePathname, useSearchParams } from 'next/navigation'

export function NavigationEvents() {
  const pathname = usePathname()
  const searchParams = useSearchParams()

  useEffect(() => {
    const url = `${pathname}?${searchParams}`
    console.log(url)
    // You can now use the current URL
    // ...
  }, [pathname, searchParams])

  return '...'
}
```

Which can be imported into a layout.

```jsx filename="app/layout.js" highlight={2,10-12}
import { Suspense } from 'react'
import { NavigationEvents } from './components/navigation-events'

export default function Layout({ children }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <body>
        {children}

        <Suspense fallback={null}>
          <NavigationEvents />
        </Suspense>
      </body>
    </html>
  )
}
```

> **Good to know**: `<NavigationEvents>` is wrapped in a [`Suspense` boundary](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading#examples) because[`useSearchParams()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-search-params) causes client-side rendering up to the closest `Suspense` boundary during [prerendering](/docs/app/glossary#prerendering). [Learn more](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-search-params#behavior).

### Disabling scroll to top

By default, Next.js will scroll to the top of the page when navigating to a new route. You can disable this behavior by passing `scroll: false` to `router.push()` or `router.replace()`.

--- title: fetch description: API reference for the extended fetch function. --- Next.js extends the [Web `fetch()` API](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Fetch_API) to allow each request on the server to set its own persistent caching and revalidation semantics. In the browser, the `cache` option indicates how a fetch request will interact with the _browser's_ HTTP cache. With this extension, `cache` indicates how a _server-side_ fetch request will interact with the framework's persistent cache. You can call `fetch` with `async` and `await` directly within Server Components. ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher export default async function Page() { let data = await fetch('https://api.vercel.app/blog') let posts = await data.json() return (
    {posts.map((post) => (
  • {post.title}
    • ))}
) } ``` ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher export default async function Page() { let data = await fetch('https://api.vercel.app/blog') let posts = await data.json() return (
    {posts.map((post) => (
  • {post.title}
    • ))}
) } ``` ## `fetch(url, options)` Since Next.js extends the [Web `fetch()` API](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Fetch_API), you can use any of the [native options available](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/fetch#parameters). ### `options.cache` Configure how the request should interact with Next.js [caching](/docs/app/getting-started/caching). ```ts fetch(`https://...`, { cache: 'force-cache' | 'no-store' }) ``` - **`auto no cache`** (default): Next.js fetches the resource from the remote server on every request in development, but will fetch once during `next build` because the route will be statically prerendered. If [Request-time APIs](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis) are detected on the route, Next.js will fetch the resource on every request. - **`no-store`**: Next.js fetches the resource from the remote server on every request, even if Request-time APIs are not detected on the route. - **`force-cache`**: Next.js looks for a matching request in its server-side cache. A request matches on its URL, method, headers, and body, so requests that differ in any of these are cached separately. - If there is a match and it is fresh, it will be returned from the cache. - If there is no match or a stale match, Next.js fetches the resource from the remote server and updates the cache with the downloaded resource. Only responses with a `200` HTTP status code are stored. > **Good to know**: Caching is opt-in. Set `cache: 'force-cache'` to cache any request, including `POST` and requests that send `authorization` or `cookie` headers. [Draft Mode](/docs/app/guides/draft-mode) bypasses the cache entirely (no read or write). ### `options.next.revalidate` ```ts fetch(`https://...`, { next: { revalidate: false | 0 | number } }) ``` Set the cache lifetime of a resource (in seconds). - **`false`** - Cache the resource indefinitely. Semantically equivalent to `revalidate: Infinity`. The HTTP cache may evict older resources over time. - **`0`** - Prevent the resource from being cached. - **`number`** - (in seconds) Specify the resource should have a cache lifetime of at most `n` seconds. > **Good to know**: > > - If an individual `fetch()` request sets a `revalidate` number lower than the [default `revalidate`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#route-segment-config-revalidate) of a route, the whole route revalidation interval will be decreased. > - If two fetch requests with the same URL in the same route have different `revalidate` values, the lower value will be used. > - Conflicting options such as `{ revalidate: 3600, cache: 'no-store' }` are not allowed, both will be ignored, and in development mode a warning will be printed to the terminal. ### `options.next.tags` ```ts

--- title: Fetching Data description: Learn how to fetch data and stream content that depends on data. related: title: Next steps description: Learn more about advanced data-fetching patterns and the features mentioned in this page. links: - app/guides/single-page-applications - app/guides/data-security - app/api-reference/functions/fetch - app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/logging - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/taint --- This page will walk you through how you can fetch data in [Server](#server-components) and [Client](#client-components) Components, and how to [stream](#streaming) components that depend on uncached data. ## Fetching data ### Server Components You can fetch data in Server Components using any asynchronous I/O, such as: 1. The [`fetch` API](#with-the-fetch-api) 2. An [ORM or database](#with-an-orm-or-database) #### With the `fetch` API To fetch data with the `fetch` API, turn your component into an asynchronous function, and await the `fetch` call. For example: ```tsx filename="app/blog/page.tsx" switcher export default async function Page() { const data = await fetch('https://api.vercel.app/blog') const posts = await data.json() return (
    {posts.map((post) => (
  • {post.title}
    • ))}
) } ``` ```jsx filename="app/blog/page.js" switcher export default async function Page() { const data = await fetch('https://api.vercel.app/blog') const posts = await data.json() return (
    {posts.map((post) => (
  • {post.title}
    • ))}
) } ``` > **Good to know:** > > - Identical `fetch` requests in a React component tree are [memoized](/docs/app/glossary#memoization) by default, so you can fetch data in the component that needs it instead of drilling props. > - `fetch` requests are not cached by default and will block the page from rendering until the request is complete. Use the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive to cache results, or wrap the fetching component in [``](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#streaming-uncached-data) to stream fresh data at request time. See [caching](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) for details. > - During development, you can log `fetch` calls for better visibility and debugging. See the [`logging` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/logging). #### With an ORM or database Since Server Components are rendered on the server, credentials and query logic will not be included in the client bundle so you can safely make database queries using an ORM or database client. ```tsx filename="app/blog/page.tsx" switcher import { db, posts } from '@/lib/db' export default async function Page() { const allPosts = await db.select().from(posts) return (
    {allPosts.map((post) => (
  • {post.title}
    • ))}
) } ``` ```jsx filename="app/blog/page.js" switcher import { db, posts } from '@/lib/db' export default async function Page() { const allPosts = await db.select().from(posts) return (
    {allPosts.map((post) => (
  • {post.title}
    • ))}
) } ``` You should still ensure requests are properly authenticated and authorized. For best practices on securing server-side data access, see the [data security guide](/docs/app/guides/data-security). ### Streaming When you fetch data in Server Components, the data is fetched and rendered on the server for each request. If you have any slow data requests, the whole route will be blocked from rendering until all the data is fetched.
