title: notFound
description: API Reference for the notFound function.
related:
  links:
    - app/api-reference/file-conventions/not-found
    - app/api-reference/functions/forbidden
    - app/api-reference/functions/unauthorized
---

The `notFound` function throws an error that renders a Next.js 404 page. It's useful for handling missing resources in your application. You can customize the UI using the [`not-found.js` file](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/not-found).

Invoking `notFound()` throws a `NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK;404` error and terminates rendering of the route segment where it was thrown. Next.js also injects a `<meta name="robots" content="noindex" />` tag so the page is not indexed. Because it works by throwing, call it in the render path: a component, or a function a component `await`s. A call left in an un-awaited promise throws where nothing catches it, and no not-found UI renders (in development the server logs `⨯ unhandledRejection: NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK;404`).

`notFound()` can be invoked in [Server Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components), [Server Functions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data), and [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).

```tsx filename="app/user/[id]/page.tsx" switcher
import { notFound } from 'next/navigation'

async function fetchUser(id: string) {
  const res = await fetch('https://...')
  if (!res.ok) return undefined
  return res.json()
}

export default async function Profile({
  params,
}: {
  params: Promise<{ id: string }>
}) {
  const { id } = await params
  const user = await fetchUser(id)

  if (!user) {
    notFound()
  }

  // ...
}
```

}

101:### Status Codes
102-
103-When streaming, a `200` status code will be returned to signal that the request was successful.
104-
105-The server can still communicate errors or issues to the client within the streamed content itself, for example, when using [`redirect`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/redirect) or [`notFound`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found). Because the response headers have already been sent to the client, the status code of the response cannot be updated.
106-
107-For example, when a 404 page is streamed to the client, Next.js includes a `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">` tag in the streamed HTML. This prevents search engines from indexing that URL even if the HTTP status is 200. See Google’s guidance on the [`robots` meta tag](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag).
108-
109-Some crawlers may label these responses as “soft 404s”. In the streaming case, this does not lead to indexation because the page is explicitly marked `noindex` in the HTML.
110-
111-If you need a 404 status, for compliance or analytics, ensure the resource exists before the response body is streamed, so that the server can set the HTTP status code.
112-
113-You can run this check in [`proxy`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy) to rewrite missing slugs to a not-found route, or [produce a 404 response](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy#producing-a-response). Keep proxy checks fast, and avoid fetching full content there.
114-
115-<details>
116-<summary>When is the response body streamed?</summary>
117-
118-The response body starts streaming when a Suspense fallback renders (for example, a `loading.tsx`) or when a Server Component suspends under a `Suspense` boundary. Place `notFound()` before those boundaries and before any `await` that may suspend.
119-
120-To start streaming, the response headers must be set. This is why it is not possible to change the status code after streaming started.
121-
122-</details>
123-
124-### Browser limits
125-
126-[Some browsers](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=252413) buffer a streaming response. You may not see the streamed response until the response exceeds 1024 bytes. This typically only affects “hello world” applications, but not real applications.
127-

129-

131-| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
132-| [Node.js server](/docs/app/getting-started/deploying#nodejs-server) | Yes               |
133-| [Docker container](/docs/app/getting-started/deploying#docker)      | Yes               |
134-| [Static export](/docs/app/getting-started/deploying#static-export)  | No                |
135-| [Adapters](/docs/app/getting-started/deploying#adapters)            | Platform-specific |

Migration complete and verified. Final state:

**Deleted** — `pages/` no longer exists: `_app.js`, `_document.js`, `_error.js`, `404.js`, `index.js`, `blog/index.js`, `blog/[id].js`, `api/posts/index.js`, `api/posts/[id].js`, plus `components/AppProvider.js` (replaced by `.tsx`).

**App Router files created**

| New file | Replaces | Key APIs |
|---|---|---|
| `app/layout.tsx` | `_app.js` + `_document.js` | `LayoutProps<'/'>`, `metadata` with `title.template`, `next/font/google` (self-hosted Inter via `--font-inter`) |
| `app/page.tsx` | `pages/index.js` + `getServerSideProps` | `await headers()`, uncached fetch |
| `app/blog/page.tsx` | `pages/blog/index.js` + `getStaticProps(revalidate: 60)` | `fetch(next:{revalidate:60})` |
| `app/blog/[id]/page.tsx` | `pages/blog/[id].js` + `getStaticProps`/`getStaticPaths` | `generateStaticParams`, `dynamicParams = true` (was `fallback:'blocking'`), `generateMetadata`, `notFound()`, `await params` |
| `app/not-found.tsx` | `pages/404.js` | `title: { absolute: … }` |
| `app/error.tsx`, `app/global-error.tsx` | `pages/_error.js` | `'use client'`, `{ error, retry }` — `retry` (v16.3+), not the discouraged `reset` |
| `app/api/posts/route.ts`, `app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts` | `pages/api/*` | Route Handlers, `RouteContext<'/api/posts/[id]'>`, `await ctx.params`, Web `Response` |
| `app/*-button.tsx` (4 files) | inline `router` usage | `'use client'` + `useRouter` from `next/navigation` |
| `lib/posts.ts`, `components/AppProvider.tsx` | — | typed fetchers (`Post`, `PostComment`), typed context |

`next/head` → Metadata API everywhere; `next/router` → `next/navigation`; the manual `res.setHeader('Allow', …)` / 405 branch is gone (framework-provided).

**Verified** (`tsc --noEmit` clean; `next build` + `next start`):
- Route classification matches the old data-fetching semantics: `ƒ /`, `○ /blog` (1m), `● /blog/1…10` (5m), `ƒ /api/posts[/[id]]`, `○ /_not-found`
- Statuses: `/` `/blog` `/blog/3` `/blog/50` → 200, `/blog/999` → **404**, `/nope` → **404** (+ `noindex`)
- Titles/descriptions/OG per route; 404 renders inside the root layout chrome; fonts served from `/_next/static/media/*.woff2` with no `fonts.googleapis.com` reference
- API: `GET /api/posts` 200, `POST` 201 / 400 (missing fields) / 400 (invalid JSON), `GET|PUT|DELETE /api/posts/7` 200 (PUT tolerates an empty body), undefined methods → 405, auto `OPTIONS` → `allow: GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, POST`

**Two deliberate tradeoffs**
1. No `app/blog/[id]/loading.tsx`. A streamed fallback forces a soft 404 (HTTP 200) because status can't change after headers flush. The old page's `router.isFallback` branch was dead code under `fallback: 'blocking'`, so nothing is lost and real 404 statuses are preserved.
2. `app/page.tsx` spells out `title: 'Home - My Blog'` rather than relying on the layout's `%s - My Blog` template — a layout template doesn't apply to a page in the same segment.

One framework behavior worth knowing: for `/blog/999` the 404 body arrives in the RSC payload (shell is `<html id="__next_error__">`) rather than as server-rendered markup, unlike `/nope`. Status, metadata and `noindex` are correct in both cases.
